pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
QUEST FOR THE ROUND TUIT

A Realm of Procrastia Adventure

In the Kingdom of Procrastia, everything gets done. Eventually. The castle in Laterburg has been waiting forty years for its roof. The bridge at Eventually Falls was started in the reign of King Dillydally VI. The Royal Library's overdue notices are themselves overdue.

What keeps the realm turning at all is the Royal Round Tuit: an old oak disc ringed in brass, kept on the Tuit Table in the Garden Court. Whenever a King of Procrastia gets a round tuit, he gets around to it. That's the law.

Then Lord Deadline, who hates a thing put off more than anything in the world, stole the Round Tuit, broke it in three and hid the pieces: one under the Snooze Barrows, one in the Soggy Vaults, one in the Putoff Mines. Without it, nobody in Procrastia gets around to anything. Least of all stopping him.

Nobody, that is, except Pip, the stable hand of Nowish, who does things the very day he's asked. His grandmother is very proud. And a little worried.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUIT and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized sound effects; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

Pick Play from the menu. Leave the menu alone and the game plays itself for a while: a good way to see how fighting works. Read Storyline tells the tale so far; Read Instructions is a short version of this manual.

Your satchel

There's nothing on the screen but Procrastia. Press F2 to open your satchel: it shows your gold, your hit points, your lives and what you carry. Save your game with F5 and load it with F6. Procrastia is bigger than it looks.

Hit points and lives

You start with 100 hit points, three lives and a single tonic. Foes bite; tonics, hearts, inn beds and the occasional pot put you right. Lose all your hit points and you start the place you're in over (with your gold and everything you've found still yours); lose all your lives and Lord Deadline wins. For now.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

↑ ↓ ← →
or W A S D		Walk. Walk into people to talk to them, into counters to buy, into gates to open them.
SpaceSwing your sword the way you last walked. Once you own a steel sword, Space swings steel.
KToot the Kazoo of Haste (once Doc Leo has taught you): a note flies straight ahead and beats nearly anything.
TDrink a tonic: 40 hit points.
EnterPick up what you're standing on. Hardly anything in Procrastia can be picked up. Hardly.
F1Help
F2Your satchel: gold, hit points, lives, what you carry
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load
EscQuit to the menu

Driving THE CHEZ

On the Dawdle Flats the arrows drive (briskly) and Space squeezes the horn: its ah-OOO-gah flies ahead like a kazoo note and clears crabs off the causeway. Your hit points are the carriage's charge. Charging posts top it up.

pages.head: Townsfolk and Shops
pages.html:
Townsfolk and Shops

To talk to someone, walk into them. They'll have their say and you'll be standing just where you were. Talk to everyone: Procrastians know a great deal and get around to telling you most of it.

Shopping

Market stalls sell from their counters. Walk into a counter once to pay, and again to take what you bought. If you can't afford it, the counter won't budge.

pages.head: The Kingdom
pages.html:
The Kingdom of Procrastia

Two lands across the Dawdle Flats, forty leagues of tidal mud nobody has ever finished walking.

Dallydale (the west)

  • Nowish: Pip's village. Population: some.
  • Laterburg: the capital. The Garden Court (roof pending), the market, the Procrastinating Pony, the Royal Library, the royal kennel.
  • Someday Harbor: on the west coast. The lighthouse, the long pier, the fishing pier, and Professor Fiddlesticks' garage.
  • The Whistling Woods, east of the River Dither, and Lake Later.

Far Putoff (the east)

  • Eventually Falls: a river town under a waterfall. Hattie's General Store, Doc Leo's tent, Foreman Duff.
  • Mount Putoff and its mines.
  • The Gloomwood, and in it Deadline Keep, where every clock has stopped at a minute to midnight.

pages.head: Foes
pages.html:
Foes

Foes come at you when you're near. A bite hurts you, but it hurts them too. Two blows finish most of them; they leave a gem behind (5 gold, or a ruby worth 20). Some things in Procrastia leave hearts.

FoeWhereNotes
ProcrastislimeEverywhereWill attack you later. Later is usually now.
Snooze BatThe hills, the Barrows, the MinesQuick. One blow.
Barrow GhostThe Snooze BarrowsDrifts through rock. Wait for it to come out.
Tide CrabThe Vaults, the FlatsSideways, always.
Bog EelThe Vaults' poolsLeaps from pool to pool.
Rust GolemThe Putoff MinesThree blows.
Gloom Goblin, Clockwork TickDeadline KeepThe Keep's staff. Underpaid. On time.

Bosses

Each piece of the Tuit is guarded by someone two blocks tall who would rather be asleep: Sir Snoozalot, the Barrow King; the Kraken of Kinda-Later; Tick-Tock the Unpunctual; and Lord Deadline himself. Your wooden sword won't scratch the last three: buy steel. Bosses sit in the way. Swing until they aren't.

pages.head: Hints
pages.html:
Hints from the Royal Library

  • Gates open for the right thing in your satchel: the Royal Writ (the Barrows), the foghorn (the fog bank on Someday Harbor's long pier), a lamp (the Mines), something with lightning in it (THE CHEZ's garage) and all three pieces (the Keep). Walk into them.
  • The King hands out writs to anyone who asks. Have two.
  • The Tuit Table in the Garden Court lights a pedestal for each piece you carry. A good way to check.
  • On the Dawdle Flats, the two low bridges flood with the tide. Wait for it to go out.
  • The rivers can't be swum. Look for bridges.
  • Shops restock whenever you come back to town.
  • Save before every boss.
  • Doc Leo's kazoo note beats nearly anything, but each toot costs a reed.
  • Waterfalls are mostly water.

Stuck? The Royal Hint Book answers everything, under a sheet of red film. Free with registration.

pages.head: Credits
pages.html:
Credits

Design, pixels, maps, music, sound and words: Claude, at Sandbox Software. Every block, monster, song and scene is a real Game-Maker 3.0 file, built in code.

The shores, rivers and roads of Procrastia are autotiles: each block is chosen by which of its four corners lie in water, road, wood or rock, and each was painted in full color with antialiased edges, foam, wet sand and shadows, then dithered into the scene's 256-color palette.

Starring

  • Doc Leo, hobo clown, PhD (Comedic Science), as himself
  • Sir Reginald Cluckington III, a rubber chicken
  • Teddy, a corgi who knows his left from his right
  • Gwinn (two n's)
  • THE CHEZ, a 1976½ CitiCar (charge port: rear passenger side)

For Lewis "Lewie" Moten III, who always gets around to it.

Made with GAME-MAKER by Recreational Software Designs.

pages.head: Registering
pages.html:
How to Register

Quest for the Round Tuit is shareware. Copy it for your friends, upload it to your favorite BBS, put it on a shareware disk: just keep all the files together and unchanged.

If you enjoy it, register for $15. You'll get:

  • the Cloth Map of Procrastia, printed on genuine imitation cloth,
  • the Royal Hint Book, with a sheet of red film to read the answers through,
  • the satisfaction of having got around to it.

Send a check or money order to:

Sandbox Software
P.O. Box 000
Pittsburgh, PA 15213

Please allow 4-6 weeks for delivery. Or, in Procrastia, 4-6 years.
